summary: Nothing new is proven this week. Last week's top item (the Spring) is built and in the playbook, and the FINRA hidden-buying gauge is live as information. The forward log has only one settled day, so the news agents can't be judged until late November. The Top 2 picks started weak (9 closed, -1.7% with stops vs -0.7% without), so the single best next step is a cheap test: replay the picks over 18 months with different stops to see whether the 1-ADR stop is costing money.

items.title: Test the Top 2 stop rule on 18 months of replayed picks
items.where: exit rule for the Top 2 picks: ledger.py stop, trade_bt.pick_replay
items.how: 5 of the first 9 live picks were stopped out and the no-stop result beat the stopped one. Replay every #1/#2 pick (with today's context re-rank) under: no stop, 1 ADR (now), 1.5 ADR, entry-day low, and close-only stops. Pick the rule only if it wins clearly; otherwise keep 1 ADR.
items.test: pick_replay from Mar 2025: next-session entry, 5-session exit, result in % and in R. Compare each stop vs the current 1-ADR stop per date, both halves same sign, t = 2 over 20+ dates; also check the worst trade and the max drawdown so a wider stop isn't just hiding risk.
items.kill: No rule beats 1 ADR in both halves, or the gain comes with much bigger worst-case losses.

items.title: Market filters on setups: volume tilt and hidden buying
items.where: playbook_state modifier (Focus - Selective on bad days); layers volume_tilt, hidden_buying
items.how: Both gauges predict SPY's next month (tilt: low outside thrusts -4.2%; FINRA S&P short share top fifth +3.1% vs +0.7%). Carried over from last week, still untested: do they change the R of OUR setups? One capture run tests both. If yes, the playbook drops every setup a notch on 'Buyers tiring' / low-hidden-buying days.
items.test: tools/picks_context/capture.py signals (5,400+), actionable 5-session result by tilt tier and by FINRA dev fifth, averaged per date, both halves, t = 2 over 20+ dates; repeat inside mixed breadth only so it isn't just the breadth regime again.
items.kill: |t| 2, halves disagree, or the effect disappears inside one breadth regime.

items.title: 'The trade' as a pick context: favour names in the winning groups when winners hold up
items.how: The 'holds up' reading is the closest thing to a pass in new research (+1.1% vs avg group, t 2.0, halves +1.3/+1.1) and the two-camps study found the same thing at the stock level (RS 90 in the winning camp +2.7% vs -5.1% when leaders sit there). Test +1 context for candidates in the winning fifth while the trade 'holds up', and -1 for the winning fifth when it 'gives back'. Two-camps is a duplicate of the_trade for building purposes; fold it in here instead of a separate tile.
items.test: Same capture signals: candidates in winning-fifth groups vs others, split by holds-up / gives-back, 5-session actionable result, per date, both halves, t = 2; then the Top 2 replay with vs without the extra context (must beat the current +1.96%/pick).
items.kill: No edge at the setup level, or it only repeats the existing ignition / leading-and-accelerating context.

items.title: In-vogue groups as long confluence for all setups
items.where: Decision-Card group layer / conviction tag on Trade Setups rows
items.how: A 6-month top-20% theme helped box longs (retest +0.22R, spring +0.45R) but has only been tested on box trades. Test it on ATH Magnet, Pullback, Rotation Rookie, Round Number, Q-Flag and VCP; if it passes, add an 'in vogue' tag that counts.
items.test: Capture signals, in vogue (6-month top-20% theme or sub-theme, as of the signal date) vs not, per setup and pooled, per date, both halves, t = 2.
items.kill: Pooled edge |t| 2 or halves disagree: keep it on box trades only.

items.title: Position ideas list: leaders in leading groups + SoW prime, 50-EMA exit, size by ADR
items.where: new list on Setups / Trade Setups (separate from the 5-day Top 2); layers position_exits, position_sizing, sow
items.how: Still the biggest unbuilt idea: top 2 by Leaders score in leading-and-accelerating sub-themes, optionally requiring SoW 'prime' or 'pop', held up to 3 months with a close-below-50-EMA exit and a size note. Its own forward log.
items.test: Exact dashboard RS/rotation/SoW code, non-overlapping monthly starts, next-open entry, vs SPY and vs other RS 70+ stocks, both halves. Only ~1 year is testable, so it can at most become information until longer history exists.
items.kill: Second half still negative vs SPY, or no better than any RS 70+ stock (the SoW pop already only beat them by +1.6%, t 1.0).

items.title: Agent layers: keep logging, first real read in late November
items.where: catalyst, calendar, macro_brief, trade_stories (forward log / story scorecard)
items.how: Nothing to build. Only Oct 15 has settled (before the agents started); the first agent-researched rows settle next week. Trade Stories is scored every day by its own price check.
items.test: Forward log: real catalyst vs none, red flag vs none, earnings in hold vs not, brief risk; t = 2 over 20+ dates, same sign both halves. Stories: favoured minus hurt groups next 5 sessions.
items.kill: No agent layer reaches |t| = 1 by ~100 settled ideas: cut the catalyst agent to earnings checks only.

items.title: Thrust follow-ups: Oct 15 shallow thrust + Oct 22 follow-through
items.how: Log the outcomes as new cases: the Oct 15 thrust was shallow and 'unconfirmed' (result lands ~Nov 13); record the post-thrust playbook's actual results after the Oct 22 follow-through.
items.kill: If Oct 15 works like a normal thrust, demote the 'unconfirmed' wording to a footnote.

retire.why: Repeat from last week: close location, absorption and fade have IC near 0 in both halves (two cards, R-2026-10-17-close-location and -who-won-the-close). The tiles take space on the Breadth tab while saying 'no forward edge found'. Keep the data columns for research.
R-2026-10-22-leaders-and-breakouts: no forward edge (|IC| = 0.2, halves disagree) over 410 days and ~40 s per build. Consider hiding the card or moving it to a collapsed section; re-test in 6 months.

IC about 0 in both halves; descriptive only.
